A daylighting film includes a first base and a plurality of daylighting portions provided on the first base. The daylighting portions are formed as polygonal prism structures, and gaps are provided between adjacent daylighting portions.

Each daylighting portion has a cross-sectional shape defined by a polygon having four vertices. All interior angles of the polygon are less than 180 degrees, so the cross-sectional shape is a convex quadrilateral. Each daylighting portion includes a first side corresponding to the surface that contacts the first base.

In the polygonal cross section, a third vertex is positioned away from the first side. Among the vertices that are not located on the first side, the third vertex has the greatest perpendicular distance from the first side. In other words, the third vertex represents the highest point of the daylighting portion relative to the surface of the first base.

The daylighting portion is not symmetrical with respect to a perpendicular line extending from the first side through the third vertex. That is, when viewed in cross section, the shape of the daylighting portion on one side of this perpendicular line differs from the shape on the other side. This asymmetrical polygonal prism structure can be used to control the direction in which incident light is refracted or guided, thereby improving daylighting performance.
outputs.L4:
A daylighting film is provided for controlling the introduction of natural light into an interior space. The film includes a first base and a plurality of daylighting portions arranged on the first base. Each daylighting portion is formed as an asymmetrical polygonal prism, and adjacent daylighting portions are spaced apart from one another by gaps. By arranging the prism structures in this manner, the film can receive incident daylight and redirect at least a portion of that light in a desired direction, thereby improving the distribution of daylight within a room or other enclosed environment.

Each asymmetrical polygonal prism has a cross-sectional shape defined by four vertices. Among these vertices, a third vertex is positioned higher than the other vertices, so that the third vertex forms a uniquely highest point of the prism cross-section. The prism is also shaped asymmetrically, meaning that the portions of the prism on opposite sides of the highest vertex are not mirror images of one another. This asymmetric configuration allows the prism to refract, reflect, or otherwise redirect incoming daylight more effectively than a symmetrical prism structure. As a result, the daylighting film can provide improved directional daylighting performance, such as by guiding sunlight deeper into an interior space, reducing glare near a window, or enhancing overall daylight utilization.
outputs.L5:
**Each**

The word **“each”** is used to talk about individual members of a group, one by one. It emphasizes that every person, object, or item is considered separately, even though they belong to the same group.

For example, in the sentence **“Each student received a book,”** the meaning is that every student got one book individually. The focus is not only on the whole class, but on every single student in it.

“Each” is often used when we want to show fairness, equality, or attention to detail. We can say:

- **Each team has a captain.**
- **Each flower in the garden is different.**
- **Each person has their own opinion.**
- **Each day brings a new opportunity.**

The word can also remind us of individuality. In a group, people may seem similar, but **each** person has unique thoughts, experiences, and abilities. This makes “each” an important word when speaking about respect and inclusion.

In everyday life, “each” helps us notice the small parts that make up a whole. Each moment, each choice, and each action can have meaning. Even small efforts, repeated each day, can lead to big results over time.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract/claim description for a daylighting film with a base layer, polygonal prism daylighting portions, and gaps, emphasizing the four-vertex cross-sectional geometry and asymmetry.
counterfactuals.output:
## Abstract

A daylighting film includes a light-transmissive base layer and a plurality of polygonal prism daylighting portions disposed on a surface of the base layer. The daylighting portions are spaced apart from one another by gaps extending along the film. Each daylighting portion has, in a cross section perpendicular to a longitudinal direction thereof, a four-vertex polygonal profile including a base-side vertex region adjacent the base layer, an outer peak vertex, and first and second lateral vertices positioned asymmetrically with respect to a centerline normal to the base layer. The four-vertex cross-sectional geometry defines a plurality of refracting and/or reflecting facets arranged to redirect incident daylight toward an interior space while suppressing glare or undesired direct transmission. The asymmetric arrangement of the lateral vertices and facets provides directional light-control characteristics that differ for light incident from different elevation angles or azimuthal directions.

## Representative Claim Description

1. A daylighting film comprising:  
   a base layer having a first major surface and a second major surface;  
   a plurality of daylighting portions disposed on the first major surface of the base layer, each daylighting portion extending in a longitudinal direction; and  
   a plurality of gaps respectively positioned between adjacent daylighting portions,  
   wherein each daylighting portion comprises a polygonal prism having a cross-sectional shape, taken in a direction perpendicular to the longitudinal direction, defined by four vertices,  
   wherein the four vertices include:  
   a first vertex positioned adjacent to the base layer;  
   a second vertex positioned outward from the base layer;  
   a third vertex positioned on a first lateral side of the daylighting portion; and  
   a fourth vertex positioned on a second lateral side of the daylighting portion,  
   and wherein the third and fourth vertices are arranged asymmetrically relative to a reference line extending through the daylighting portion in a thickness direction of the base layer.

2. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein the four vertices define four side facets configured to refract, reflect, or totally internally reflect incident sunlight.

3. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein the second vertex is laterally offset from a midpoint of a width of the daylighting portion.

4. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein at least one of the third and fourth vertices is positioned at a different height from the other relative to the first major surface of the base layer.

5. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein the gaps comprise air gaps, resin-filled gaps, or recessed regions between adjacent polygonal prism daylighting portions.

6. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein the asymmetric four-vertex cross-sectional shape is configured to redirect daylight incident at a high solar elevation angle toward a ceiling or upper interior region of a building.

7. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein each daylighting portion has a substantially constant cross-sectional shape along the longitudinal direction.

8. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein the base layer and the daylighting portions are integrally formed from a transparent or translucent polymeric material.

9. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein the daylighting portions are periodically arranged at a predetermined pitch, and wherein each gap has a gap width smaller than, equal to, or greater than a width of a corresponding daylighting portion.

10. The daylighting film of claim 1, wherein the asymmetry of the four-vertex cross-sectional shape causes the daylighting film to exhibit different optical redirection characteristics depending on an orientation of the film relative to a light source.

## Additional Patent-Style Description

In one embodiment, the daylighting film includes a transparent base film and a plurality of elongated prism structures formed on one side of the transparent base film. The prism structures are separated by intervening gaps so that optical interfaces are formed between each prism structure and an adjacent medium. Each prism structure has a quadrilateral cross-sectional outline rather than a conventional triangular prism profile. The quadrilateral outline includes four distinct vertex portions connected by four facets. The relative positions of the vertices are selected so that the prism profile is not mirror-symmetric about a thickness-direction centerline of the prism.

The asymmetric quadrilateral prism profile may include a steep incident-side facet and a comparatively shallow exit-side facet, or vice versa, depending on the intended mounting orientation. In use, sunlight entering the daylighting film is refracted at one or more facets and may be internally reflected at another facet before exiting the film in a controlled direction. By adjusting the positions of the four vertices, including the lateral offset of the outer vertex and/or the unequal heights of the lateral vertices, the film can preferentially redirect daylight upwardly into a room while reducing direct glare toward occupants.

The gaps between adjacent daylighting portions may enhance optical separation between the prism structures, provide additional refractive interfaces, reduce optical coupling, or permit controlled deformation or manufacturing tolerance. The base layer may function as a supporting substrate, a window-adhering layer, or an optical transmission layer. The daylighting portions may be formed by embossing, casting, extrusion, ultraviolet-curable resin replication, or another microstructured-film manufacturing process.
